rules.treatment: No price adjustment on ex-date; the Price Return index is not adjusted (PAF = none).
Reinvests the cash dividend on ex-date in the Gross Daily Total Return index.
Reinvests the cash dividend on ex-date in the Net Daily Total Return index.

Classified special and PR-adjusted via PAF = (CumPx − Div) / CumPx only when the dividend is ≥5% of market price; below 5% it is treated as ordinary with no PR adjustment. TR/NTR indexes reinvest regardless of classification.
Treated identically to a stock split: PAF padj = pt-1 × A / (A+B); no divisor change; PR index adjusted.
No price adjustment; shares multiplied by the bonus ratio; market cap unchanged; no divisor adjustment.
PAF padj = pt-1 × A / (A+B); divisor unchanged; market cap unchanged.
Child added as a detached security at the when-issued price when available, else zero, held until a real price is available; parent's value deducted on ex-date.

For in-the-money rights (subscription price below market), applies a PAF using the theoretical ex-rights price (TERP). Shares are increased as of the close of ex-date; NOS/FIF/DIF changes use 5%/10%/25% thresholds for Standard/Small/Micro cap tiers.
For out-of-the-money rights (subscription price greater than or equal to market price on ex-date), reflects the rights issue by applying a PAF of 1; no price adjustment is made.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/msci-corporate-events-methodology-feb-2026.pdf §3.6.1.2 (Rights for new underlying shares, premium to market price)

rules.treatment: Applied (PAF + divisor) when the share-count change meets the size threshold — ≥5% of pre-event NOS for Standard, ≥10% Small Cap, ≥25% Micro Cap — with 2 full business days advance notice; changes <±1% on post-event NOS deferred to the next Index Review.

New shares counted toward NOS; adjustment applied when the change meets the size threshold (≥5%/10%/25% by cap tier), with a simultaneous primary + private placement sized jointly; changes <±1% on post-event NOS deferred to the next Index Review.

Treated as a special dividend: extraordinary (vs dividend policy/history) → PAF applied using the gross amount and reinvested in DTR indexes; regular → treated as a normal cash dividend, reinvested in DTR indexes regardless of size.
Target deleted when the deal is unconditional (no fixed % threshold), at last traded price; acquirer share-count change triggers adjustment at 5%/10%/25% by Standard/Small/Micro cap tier.

Deletion when the tender offer is formally completed (no % acceptance threshold and no advance notice — MSCI waits for completion rather than deleting at an acceptance level); removed at tender price or last traded price.

Deleted as soon as possible on a bankruptcy / protection-from-creditors filing when a return to normal business is unlikely; removed at the last traded price, else an OTC / equivalent market price, else the lowest system price (0.00001), with 2 full business days notice.
An ordinary dividend has no effect on the Price Return index; no price adjustment is made on ex-date (PAF = none).
An ordinary dividend affects the Total Return (TR) index; the dividend is reinvested on ex-date.
An ordinary dividend affects the Net Total Return (NTR) index; the dividend is reinvested on ex-date.

Treated as a corporate action with price and divisor adjustment: the stock's price is adjusted (reduced) by the payment amount at the opening of the effective date. Classification is qualitative — outside the normal historical payment pattern (e.g. described as "special", "extra", "irregular", or "return of capital"); the third consecutive same-timing non-ordinary dividend is reclassified as ordinary (timing, not amount).
Treated identically to a stock split: shares increased and price decreased by the same adjustment factor (e.g. a 5% stock dividend is a 1.05-for-1 split). Market capitalization unchanged.

Treated identically to a stock split / stock dividend: shares increased and price decreased by the same factor, with only the quoting convention differing. Bonus shares not entitled to a later dividend are applied on ex-date, with the later dividend adjusted down over the enlarged share count.
Shares increased (multiplied) and price decreased (divided) by the same adjustment factor; market capitalization unchanged; no divisor change.

Spin-off security added to the parent's indices at a zero price at the close of the day before the ex-date, with no divisor adjustment; the parent is not price-adjusted downward. If the spin-off does not trade for 20 consecutive trading days after the ex-date, it may be removed at zero.

For in-the-money rights (subscription price below the stock closing price on the day before the ex-date), applies a price adjustment using the theoretical ex-rights price (TERP) at the opening of the ex-date and increases shares at the full rights ratio. If undersubscribed or oversubscribed, the corresponding share adjustment is made at the next quarterly share rebalancing.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/sp-equity-indices-policies-practices.pdf §Rights Offerings; §S&P DJI’s Calculation of Rights Offerings, Step 1–2

rules.treatment: For out-of-the-money rights (subscription price greater than or equal to the stock closing price on the day before the ex-date), takes no action to match the corporate action for index purposes; any subsequent shares are made at the quarterly rebalancing.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/sp-equity-indices-policies-practices.pdf §S&P DJI’s Calculation of Rights Offerings, Step 1–2

rules.treatment: Public offerings (including block sales and spot secondaries) receive accelerated implementation only when both thresholds are met: at least 5% of pre-event shares and at least US$150m (a US$1bn+ event is implemented even below 5%). Otherwise implemented at the next quarterly rebalancing.
Non-mandatory; certain private placements are reviewed quarterly and implemented at the quarterly rebalancing, not via accelerated implementation.

Considered a special dividend (price adjusted down at the opening of the effective date), except when declared in lieu of an ordinary cash dividend and fitting the historical pattern in amount and frequency, in which case it is treated as an ordinary cash dividend.

Target deleted on or around the expected delisting or last-trading date, with no minimum threshold for the acquirer's share/IWF change; deletion price is the closing price, or for cash consideration the lower of market close and deal price, for stock consideration a synthetically derived price from the deal ratio. Acquisitions of private/non-index companies are implemented at the next quarterly rebalancing.

Index changes implemented only after final results. A target may be removed early once conditions are met or when remaining free float falls below 15% (even if the offer is still open); the tendered-line replacement is considered once a minimum acceptance ratio of 75% is reached, with one to five business days' notice.
Bankrupt securities are ineligible and removed from all branded indices simultaneously, with a minimum of one day's notice, at the primary-exchange closing price (zero if halted or delisted).

Ordinary cash dividends have no price adjustment or PAF; the Price Return index is unchanged. Cash (and scrip) dividends with a cash option are treated the same as ordinary cash, except Spanish scrip dividends, which follow the scrip-issue treatment (§4.7).
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends); §4.3 (Unknown and optional ordinary dividends and corrections); §4.8.1 (Cash dividends table)

rules.treatment: Ordinary cash dividends are reinvested across the index on the ex date and affect the Total Return index. Cash (and scrip) dividends with a cash option are treated the same as ordinary cash, except Spanish scrip dividends, which follow the scrip-issue treatment (§4.7). Where a dividend is retracted or corrected, a corrective negative adjustment is applied with T+1 notice; an undetermined dividend uses the same-period prior-year amount, or zero if none was paid.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends); §4.3 (Unknown and optional ordinary dividends and corrections); §4.8.1 (Cash dividends table)

rules.treatment: Special cash dividends are classified by the company description, not by amount, and the stock price is adjusted to deduct the dividend amount before the open on the ex date. A recurring special dividend paid on more than three consecutive non-extraordinary occasions is reclassified as ordinary on the fourth.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.4 (Special dividends – tax adjustments)

rules.treatment: Special cash dividends are excluded from the Total Return index calculation. They are classified by the company description, not by amount; a recurring special dividend paid on more than three consecutive non-extraordinary occasions is reclassified as ordinary on the fourth.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.4 (Special dividends – tax adjustments)

rules.treatment: Special cash dividends are excluded from the return calculation; where the distribution is at least 10% of cum price and has withholding-tax implications, FTSE Russell applies a compensating negative XD adjustment to net-of-tax indices only. Classification is by company description, not amount.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.4 (Special dividends – tax adjustments)

rules.treatment: Treated as a scrip issue / stock distribution (§4.7): automatic distribution of shares (existing or newly issued) at no charge pro rata to holdings, with a price adjustment factor of shares held before ÷ after; no index divisor adjustment and no change in market capitalisation.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.7 (Scrip issues & stock distributions)

rules.treatment: Treated as a scrip issue (capitalisation / bonus issue) (§4.7): shares distributed at no charge pro rata to existing holdings; the price adjustment factor (shares held before ÷ after) is applied on the ex date; no index divisor adjustment and no change in market capitalisation.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.7 (Scrip issues & stock distributions)

rules.treatment: No index divisor adjustment; the price adjustment factor is shares held before ÷ after (e.g. 0.2 for a 1-into-5 split); applied on the ex date with no change in company market capitalisation.

Parent is price-adjusted by way of a capital repayment; the spun-off entity is added to the same indices as the parent on the ex date at an estimated price using the hierarchy: when-issued price, primary-exchange estimate, company valuation, broker estimate, then the terms of the action. If the spin-off has not traded within 20 business days of the ex date and no firm trading date is announced, it is normally deleted at zero with T+2 notice. Withholding-tax obligations ≥10% of share price trigger a compensating negative XD adjustment to net-of-tax indices only.

Only in-the-money rights (subscription price below market) are recognised: a price adjustment factor (theoretical ex-rights price ÷ cum-rights price) and share increase are applied before the open on the ex date. Terms greater than 10-for-1 are ‘highly dilutive’ and use temporary rights and subscription-cash lines until the subscription period ends; this separate dilution-ratio branch is not representable by the current conditions vocabulary. Where the subscription price is unknown on the ex date an estimated value is used, or no adjustment if it cannot be estimated.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.9 (Rights issues/entitlement offers); §4.9.3 (Highly dilutive rights issues); §4.9.9 (Rights issue summary)

rules.treatment: Rights with a subscription price equal to or above the market price are not adjusted or increased on the ex date; any additional shares are reviewed for inclusion at the next quarterly review.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.9 (Rights issues/entitlement offers); §4.9.9 (Rights issue summary)

rules.treatment: Share and free-float updates from primary and secondary offerings are implemented intra-quarter with at least two days' notice when they meet the materiality threshold — a USD 1bn investable market-cap change, or a 5% index-shares change plus USD 250m — otherwise deferred to the next quarterly review (or the review following discovery if pricing settled more than five business days earlier).
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §5.2 (Intra-quarter updates); §2.1.5 (Timing of corporate actions and events)

rules.treatment: Share and free-float changes from private placements to restricted parties are deferred to the next quarterly review; they do not qualify for the intra-quarter primary/secondary-offering treatment and receive no intra-quarter price or share adjustment.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §5 (Changes to shares outstanding and free float), note 5

rules.treatment: Capital repayments are generally applied with a price adjustment (capital-repayment PAF = (price − repayment) ÷ price), unless company policy reports regular dividends this way (common in Switzerland), in which case it is treated as an ordinary cash dividend.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.8.1 (Capital repayment table)

rules.treatment: Capital repayments are not included in the Total Return index calculation; they generally receive a capital-repayment price adjustment unless company policy reports regular dividends this way (common in Switzerland), in which case they are treated as ordinary cash dividends.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.8.1 (Capital repayment table)

rules.treatment: Target is deleted at the last traded price and the acquirer's shares increased per the offer terms once the transaction is deemed final, with a minimum two days' notice; where trading in the target has halted, a synthetic price based on the offer terms is used. For mergers involving elections, FTSE Russell generally waits for the election results before implementing.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.10.2 (Merger between index constituents for stock); §2.1.5 (minimum two-day notice for stock and cash mergers)

rules.treatment: Target normally removed with a minimum T+2 notice when the bidder's holding reaches at least 90% (initial, extension or subsequent) with shares irrevocably accepted for payment, or remaining free float is under 5%, or a compulsory squeeze-out / delisting is confirmed; otherwise a free-float change greater than 3 percentage points is implemented with at least T+2 notice. Deleted at the last traded price, or at a price based on the offer terms if trading has halted.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.11 (Target company deletion); §4.12 (Target company free float change)

rules.treatment: Deleted when FTSE Russell becomes aware of bankruptcy / protection-from-creditors filing, administration, receivership, insolvency or liquidation, with notice — bankruptcy is an ‘actionable’ event carrying a minimum two-day notice. Removed at the last traded price, or an OTC/ineligible-market price if available, else a nominal 0.0001; re-considered after 12 months as a new issue (Russell US and derived indices re-consider at the next reconstitution).

Ordinary cash distributions within the regular dividend policy (or defined regular by the company) adjust Gross and Net Return indices, while Price indices are not affected: no price adjustment and no PAF for the Price Return index.

Cash distributions outside the regular dividend policy (or defined extraordinary by the company) adjust Gross Return, Net Return, and Price indices; Net Return and Price use padj = pt−1 − Div × (1−withholding tax). STOXX states no numeric special-dividend threshold: classification is qualitative, based on dividend policy or company characterization.

An ordinary stock dividend decreases the price by the pre-/post-distribution share ratio and increases shares by the reciprocal ratio for free-float market-cap indices; the divisor is unchanged. Treasury-stock and redeemable-share distributions instead follow regular or special cash-dividend treatment according to classification.

A pro-rata no-charge share distribution is treated as an ordinary stock dividend: price is decreased by the pre-/post-distribution share ratio, shares rise by the reciprocal ratio for free-float market-cap indices, and the divisor is unchanged.
For a split or reverse split, price is adjusted by A/B and free-float market-cap shares by B/A; the divisor is unchanged.

The parent price is reduced by the value of spun-off shares. Each spin-off stock is temporarily added to affected indices at an estimated price where eligible-exchange listing, pricing, and reference data are available; a non-qualifying spin-off is deleted when it starts trading. Changes are announced immediately, implemented two trading days later, and effective the following trading day.

Only in-the-money rights are adjusted: the theoretical ex-rights price is applied and shares increase. If the subscription price is unavailable or at/above the prior close, no adjustment is made. A rights issue with B/A ≥200% is highly dilutive and follows the stated underwriting/tradability scenarios.

A share-count change from a corporate action greater than ±10% from one trading day to the next is announced immediately, implemented two trading days later, and effective the following trading day; other applicable changes follow the quarterly underlying-data schedule. Free-float factor changes over ±5 percentage points use the same two-day process.

A share-count change from a corporate action greater than ±10% from one trading day to the next is announced immediately, implemented two trading days later, and effective the following trading day; other applicable changes follow the quarterly underlying-data schedule. Free-float factor changes over ±5 percentage points use the same two-day process.

A return of capital with share consolidation is applied as a combination of a regular or special cash dividend and a reverse split. Regular classification uses the regular-dividend return-index treatment plus split treatment for Price indices; special classification applies special-dividend treatment to Price, Gross Return, and Net Return indices plus split treatment.

A merger or takeover deletes the target once event conditions are fulfilled and at least 85% is acquired through the tender offer or remaining target free float is below 10%. Changes are announced immediately, implemented two trading days later, and effective the following trading day; use last traded price or an acquisition-terms artificial price if not trading.

Following publication of each tender-offer result (including an extension), STOXX makes an extraordinary target free-float adjustment if approvals and minimum acceptance are fulfilled and free float changes by at least 5 percentage points; deletion follows if all event conditions are fulfilled and at least 85% is acquired or remaining free float is below 10%. Changes are announced immediately, implemented two trading days later, and effective the following trading day.

A company that files for bankruptcy is deleted during ongoing bankruptcy proceedings at its primary-market traded price, if available, otherwise at local-currency 0.0000001. Changes are announced immediately, implemented two trading days later, and effective the following trading day.
No price adjustment for ordinary cash dividends; the Price Return (PR) index is not adjusted (PAF = none).
Reinvests gross ordinary dividends in the Total Return (TR) index; gross dividends are used in calculating TR index levels.
Reinvests net ordinary dividends in the Net Return (NR) index; net dividends are used in calculating NR index levels after tax.

A non-ordinary cash distribution of at least 5% of the underlying security’s market price when announced in finalized status is treated as a special dividend: the price is reduced at the effective-date opening and PAF = adjusted price / prior close. Non-ordinary distributions below 5% are ordinary; M&A prepayments and spin-off cash payments are special regardless of size.

Treated as a stock split: index shares increase and price decreases by the stock-dividend ratio, leaving the security’s index market value unchanged. Index-ineligible distributed instruments are not recognized.

Treated the same as a stock dividend: shares increase and price decreases by the bonus ratio; bonus rights issues with only stock options receive the same treatment. If bonus shares are not entitled to a later dividend, that dividend is adjusted over the enlarged share count.

Index shares increase and the price decreases by the stock-split ratio, leaving the security’s index market value unchanged; PAF = pre-event total shares outstanding / post-event total shares outstanding.

A newly created spin-off is added at zero price without divisor adjustment and removed with a divisor adjustment after at least two regular trading days. If it has not traded for 40 trading days after ex-date and has no listing information, it may be removed at zero with client notice (60 days for India); publicly listed distributions use a zero-price placeholder.
For in-the-money rights (positive value of right), applies the theoretical ex-right price (TERP) and Price Adjustment Factor (PAF), and increases index shares.
For at- or out-of-the-money rights (zero or negative value of right), makes no corporate-action adjustment; rights issuing index-ineligible instruments are not recognized.

Public/secondary offerings are nonmandatory. Material share and corresponding float changes are accelerated weekly when the offering exceeds both USD 150m and 5% of shares, or exceeds USD 1bn even below 5%; otherwise qualifying changes are implemented at quarterly rebalancing. A subscription offer to existing holders follows the rights-offering treatment.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/morningstar-corporate-action-methodology-2026.pdf §Corporate Action Category (p. 5); §Subscription Offer (p. 22); §Nonmandatory Corporate Action Methodology (p. 37)

rules.treatment: Private placements are nonmandatory; material share and corresponding float changes follow the nonmandatory accelerated weekly policy when they meet its stated thresholds, with non-material qualifying changes implemented at quarterly rebalancing.

Generally nonrecurring and treated as a special dividend under the special-dividend price-threshold treatment. It is treated as an ordinary cash dividend only when declared in lieu of an ordinary dividend and its amount and frequency fit the historical ordinary-dividend pattern.

The target is generally deleted from all indexes on or around delisting (or earlier once it can no longer be acquired). Acquirer share/free-float changes depend on cash versus stock terms; if the target is halted, removal uses the cash tender price or derived stock deal price.

Morningstar monitors public tender-offer results; it may replace a tendered share class after 75% acceptance during a further acceptance period. It may drop the target with a two-day client notice when delisting/suspension is confirmed, 90% of shares are tendered or float is below 10%, or the offer is unconditional / headed to compulsory acquisition.

Bankrupt or financially distressed securities are ineligible and removed with a minimum two days’ notice: at the usual/primary-exchange closing price if trading, otherwise zero; for U.S. securities, use OTC/pink-sheet price when available before zero.
No index divisor adjustment; the price adjustment factor is shares held before ÷ after, applied on the ex-date with no change in company market capitalisation.
Regular Cash Dividends are neglected in a Price Return Index; no price adjustment or PAF is made for the regular cash distribution.
Gross Total Return Indexes reinvest Cash and Special Dividend distributions without deducting withholding tax.
Net Total Return Indexes reinvest Cash and Special Dividend distributions after deducting withholding tax.
Special Dividends are included in a Price Return Index; regular Cash Dividends are the distributions neglected by the Price Return variant.
Gross Total Return Indexes reinvest Special Dividend distributions without deducting withholding tax.
Net Total Return Indexes reinvest Special Dividend distributions after deducting withholding tax.

A Stock Dividend applies a PAF of 1 + stock terms, lowers the theoretical price proportionally, and increases index shares by the same factor; it is treated identically in Standard and Divisor Indices with no Divisor change.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/solactive-equity-index-methodology-v1.20-2026-06-16.pdf v1.20 (2026-06-16; sha256:e11e20f81b211862711f0ac519604e04155ed9293294cb5fe207b3cf470db1fb) §2.1.2 Stock Dividend; §2.1.2.1 Stock Dividend Adjustment (pp.19–20)

rules.treatment: Mapped to the Solactive Stock Dividend treatment: a pro-rata no-charge share distribution is adjusted with the stock-distribution PAF and corresponding shares; the source does not publish a separately named Bonus Issue rule.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/solactive-equity-index-methodology-v1.20-2026-06-16.pdf v1.20 (2026-06-16; sha256:e11e20f81b211862711f0ac519604e04155ed9293294cb5fe207b3cf470db1fb) §2.1.2 Stock Dividend; §2.1.2.1 Stock Dividend Adjustment (pp.19–20)
rules.mapping_note: App event bonus-issue is mapped to the methodology's stock-dividend treatment because both describe a pro-rata additional-share distribution; no separate Bonus Issue section is published.

rules.treatment: Stock Splits and Reverse Stock Splits preserve company market capitalization by changing shares and price proportionally; the adjustment follows the Stock Split methodology.

The spin-off company is added on the effective date with shares from the transaction terms; it starts at zero or a calculated theoretical price until official trading, while the parent remains. An ineligible or non-tradable distribution can instead be treated as an extraordinary dividend, temporary addition/removal, or non-event under the stated alternatives.

A Rights Issue is implemented only when the subscription price is below the stock close price on the day before the ex-date; the PAF/TERP-style adjustment and share treatment then follow the Standard or Divisor formula.

rules.source_ref: SOURCES/solactive-equity-index-methodology-v1.20-2026-06-16.pdf v1.20 (2026-06-16; sha256:e11e20f81b211862711f0ac519604e04155ed9293294cb5fe207b3cf470db1fb) §2.1 Corporate Actions (p.12; no dedicated secondary-offering treatment published)

SOURCES/solactive-equity-index-methodology-v1.20-2026-06-16.pdf v1.20 (2026-06-16; sha256:e11e20f81b211862711f0ac519604e04155ed9293294cb5fe207b3cf470db1fb) §2.1 Corporate Actions (p.12; no dedicated private-placement treatment published)

rules.treatment: Return of capital is generally applied as a special dividend free of withholding tax; when repetitive in amount and frequency and paid in lieu of a regular Cash Dividend, it is classified as an ordinary Cash Dividend. No numeric threshold is stated.

Under the general Solactive framework, the target is removed on the effective date. For an index-component acquirer, cash terms redistribute the target weight pro rata, stock terms increase the surviving shares, and mixed terms split those treatments; for a non-component acquirer, the target weight is redistributed for all listed terms. An Index Guideline supersedes this framework when it differs, so this is not universal product coverage.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/solactive-equity-index-methodology-v1.20-2026-06-16.pdf v1.20 (2026-06-16; sha256:e11e20f81b211862711f0ac519604e04155ed9293294cb5fe207b3cf470db1fb) §2.1.7 Mergers & Acquisitions; §2.1.7.1 Mergers & Acquisition Adjustment (pp.26–27)

rules.treatment: Mapped from Solactive's takeover/tender-offer M&A treatment: a target is removed when the stated M&A timing conditions are met, including delisting, squeeze-out, or a successful unconditional offer with free float below 15%; at least two Business Days notice is stated. An Index Guideline may supersede this framework.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/solactive-equity-index-methodology-v1.20-2026-06-16.pdf v1.20 (2026-06-16; sha256:e11e20f81b211862711f0ac519604e04155ed9293294cb5fe207b3cf470db1fb) §2.1.7 Mergers & Acquisitions; §2.1.7.2 Timing of Adjustment (pp.26–32)
rules.mapping_note: App event tender-offer is mapped to the methodology's takeover-offer branch in M&A; Solactive does not publish a separate Tender Offer section in this framework.

rules.treatment: Bankruptcy, insolvency, or liquidation triggers removal after the last trading day with at least two Business Days notice. Last close or an official alternative-market price is used; if no robust price exists, 0.00000001 is used, and weight is redistributed only when a determined price is available. Bankruptcy protection alone does not satisfy the removal condition unless delisting is announced.
Regular cash dividends do not adjust the Price Return index.
Regular cash dividends are applied on the ex-date to the Gross Total Return variant; the policy states dividends are reinvested in total-return indexes.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/vettafi-index-maintenance-policy-v1.1.8-2026-05.pdf v1.1.8 (May 2026; sha256:7470738f689760f0bbd64d0ecb95b7248fdf05ba35b9c0a340e9e967be881c7a) §8 Treatment of Distributions; §9 Regular Cash Dividends; §II.1 Index Formula (pp.3,5)

rules.treatment: Regular cash dividends are applied on the ex-date to the Net Total Return variant; the policy states dividends are reinvested in total-return indexes.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/vettafi-index-maintenance-policy-v1.1.8-2026-05.pdf v1.1.8 (May 2026; sha256:7470738f689760f0bbd64d0ecb95b7248fdf05ba35b9c0a340e9e967be881c7a) §9 Regular Cash Dividends; §II.1 Index Formula (pp.3,5)

rules.treatment: For a market-cap-weighted index, the security price is reduced by the special dividend and proceeds are redistributed proportionally to remaining constituents. The adjustment applies to Price, Total Return, and Net Total Return variants.

For a non-market-cap-weighted index, the security price is reduced by the special dividend and proceeds are reinvested into the payer by increasing index shares so the weight is unchanged. The adjustment applies to Price, Total Return, and Net Total Return variants.

Stock dividends increase index shares and reduce security price proportionally; constituent weight is unchanged. The divisor/formula table gives adjusted price = closing price × A/(A+B) and new shares = old shares × (A+B)/A.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/vettafi-index-maintenance-policy-v1.1.8-2026-05.pdf v1.1.8 (May 2026; sha256:7470738f689760f0bbd64d0ecb95b7248fdf05ba35b9c0a340e9e967be881c7a) §6 Stock Splits and Stock Dividends; §III.6 Stock Dividend (pp.2,8–9)

rules.treatment: Mapped to VettaFi's Stock Dividend treatment: the policy does not publish a separately named Bonus Issue rule, but its stock-distribution formula covers the same pro-rata no-charge share-distribution mechanics.

rules.treatment: For a market-cap-weighted index, the parent price is reduced by the spin-off value, the parent remains, and the spin-off is initially dropped with its weight redistributed; if value is unknown, it is added at zero and removed after two trading days.

For a non-market-cap-weighted index, the parent price is reduced by the spin-off value and parent shares increase to keep weight unchanged; an unknown-value spin-off is added at zero, removed after two trading days, and its weight transfers to the parent.

Rights are exercised only when the subscription price is below the prior-day close (in-the-money); price is adjusted downward by rights value, shares increase on full terms, and exercise costs come proportionally from remaining constituents.

Rights are exercised only when the subscription price is below the prior-day close (in-the-money); price is adjusted downward by rights value and shares increase to offset the price decrease so weight remains unchanged.

rules.treatment: Merger treatment is index-specific, not universal: Approach 1.0 transfers weight to a surviving component, Approach 2.0 redistributes it to remaining constituents, and Approach 3.0 depends on cash/stock terms. Approaches 1.0/2.0 are defaults by weighting; Approach 3.0 applies to listed indexes in the Appendix. A product methodology is required to resolve the applicable approach.

rules.treatment: A component delisted from all eligible exchanges is removed with weight reallocated; a component entering bankruptcy is removed and remains ineligible until emergence, subject to Committee review. If price is unavailable, use alternate exchange/OTC sources in the stated order; if no traded price or bid/ask range exists and the security is worthless or too illiquid, remove it at 0.01 local currency.
